title: Multi-consumer stream shim for consistent async-iterator and Web Streams semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
proposed_solution: Implement a CheckpointedStream wrapper around the canonical internal stream object with: (1) an internal ring buffer for recent chunks with reference counting by checkpoint; (2) explicit createCheckpoint()/releaseCheckpoint() API; (3) toAsyncIterator() and toWebStream() conversion helpers that preserve cancellation semantics; (4) backpressure hooks that pause the underlying transport when no consumers are actively reading; (5) a minimal ownership API (claim() / clone()) for consumers that need exclusive vs shared reads.
design_decisions: Use lightweight in-memory ring buffer instead of full buffering to avoid O(streamSize) memory; keep retention window configurable via sdk config.
Reference-counted checkpoints give predictable retention but require explicit release() calls in user code; provide automatic release on iterator completion and on stream cancel to reduce footguns.
Expose both toAsyncIterator() and toWebStream() on the same wrapper to reduce glue code in client apps and ensure both surfaces share the same lifecycle.
Do not attempt automatic server replay or checkpoint reconciliation; server-side replay is out of scope for this ticket.
Favor clear semantics over magic: claim() semantics will transfer exclusive ownership; clone() will create a shared-reader from the current head position.
Backpressure: if all consumers are slow or paused we will surface a TCP-level/transport-level pause hook to avoid OOM on high-throughput producers.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover: single consumer iteration, conversion to WebStream, two concurrent consumers with checkpoint usage, explicit claim() transfer, and cancellation propagation.
Integration test in browser fixture verifying toWebStream().getReader() backpressure behavior and cancel() signals propagate to underlying connection.
A benchmark shows memory retention stays within configured window for a 10k token stream with two checkpoints created mid-stream.
Type definitions compile cleanly and examples added to docs/ts-sdk/streams.md and example repo.
PR with implementation and tests merged and a followup task filed for API stabilization notes.
